niche: online spiritual and shadow work courses
prompt_text: What are the best online courses for learning shadow work and spiritual practice?
answer_verbatim:
“Best” depends on whether you want a psychology-informed approach, a regular contemplative practice, or both. These are good places to start:

### Shadow work
- **[Jung Platform — *Encounters with the Shadow*](https://jungplatform.com/course/encounters-with-the-shadow)** — A structured introduction to Jungian shadow work, with video and audio lessons and a companion guide. A strong first choice if you want a depth-psychology framework.
- **[Jung Platform — shadow courses](https://jungplatform.com/shadow-work)** — A broader collection of courses and talks, including material from Jungian analysts and depth psychologists. Useful if you want to explore different perspectives after an introductory course.
- **[Udemy — *Shadow Work: Heal & Integrate your Shadow Self*](https://www.udemy.com/course/shadow_work/)** — A self-paced option. Course quality can vary on large marketplaces, so check the instructor’s background, syllabus, reviews, and refund terms before buying.

### Spiritual practice
- **[Naropa University / The Awake Network — *Mindfulness: What It Is, Where It Comes From, and How to Practice It*](https://www.naropa.edu/academics/personal-enrichment/)** — A free introductory course that connects mindfulness practice with its Buddhist roots.
- **[Mindworks — online mindfulness courses](https://mindworks.org/meditation-courses/mindfulness-courses/)** — A practical option for learning meditation and awareness through guided instruction.
- **[Sounds True — spiritual healing courses](https://www.soundstrue.com/collections/spiritual-healing-courses)** — A wide range of courses involving meditation, breathwork, compassion, and other contemplative practices. Choose based on the specific practice and teacher you’re interested in.

**A sensible path:** start with Naropa’s free mindfulness course, then try *Encounters with the Shadow* if you want to explore shadow work. Look for clear learning goals, transparent instructor credentials, and exercises you can approach at your own pace.

Shadow work can bring up difficult emotions. It’s best treated as reflective learning—not a substitute for therapy—and you can pause or seek support if the exercises feel overwhelming.
